corsSpike.summary: Both target ArcGIS Server instances return permissive, origin-reflecting CORS headers on real /query and /exportImage calls, not just on service-root probes. esriFeature (client-side interactive vector) is viable directly against both servers — the esriDynamic/harvest fallback is not required as a default, only as an option for oversized or historical layer sets.

corsSpike.method: curl -D - -H "Origin: http://localhost:8000" against real query/export endpoints on each server, inspecting response headers for Access-Control-Allow-Origin/Access-Control-Allow-Credentials. This is a decisive, reproducible proxy for browser CORS enforcement (the browser applies the exact same header check); a live-browser confirmation from the actual served site is a cheap final sanity check worth doing once in Phase 3 but is not expected to change this result.
corsSpike.conclusion: Default sourceType for interactive Iberia/CIMS feature layers can be esriFeature. Reserve esriDynamic for layers that are visually dense but don't need per-feature interactivity (e.g., yearly historical shoreline contour stacks), and reserve harvested geojson for anything CORS-blocked in the future or for the parish boundary clip mask itself (small, static, worth freezing rather than re-fetching).

candidateLayers.harvestNotes: CORRECTION, found live while writing tools/gis-harvest.mjs (task 3.13, 2026-08-02): the 'per-year contour layers back to 1870s' referenced just above (lasard/contoursYYYY, e.g. lasard/contours1934) are NOT shoreline position snapshots — checked live, they're TopoBathyContours: bathymetric/topographic elevation isolines (Z_FT class-break renderer, fields like V_BENCH/V_EPOCH/THICKNESS) mined near each labelled year, not the shoreline itself. Wrong dataset for a coastal-change time slider. Harvested lasard/shoreline instead (the same layer already CORS/query-verified above) — a single compiled feature layer where each feature carries its own SRC_DATE (YYYYMMDD), not one shoreline per calendar year. Real coverage inside the Iberia envelope clusters unevenly: dense around 1931-1937, 1946-1955, 1994-1999, then solid single-year counts in 2008 and 2015 — so the 'five representative years' are SRC_DATE range windows (1930-1939→'1935', 1945-1955→'1948', 1994-1999→'1998', plus exact 2008 and 2015), not five clean single-date queries. Each window queried with the parish-envelope spatial filter, then features were genuinely clipped (not just kept-or-dropped) to the vertex runs falling inside the real parish polygon — one 1998-window feature (USGS DDS-79, a statewide digitization) had 475,623 vertices before clipping trimmed it to only its Iberia-intersecting run. Simplified with Ramer-Douglas-Peucker at 0.0001° (~10m) after clipping, coordinates rounded to 6 decimals. Final sizes: 110-610KB per file, all well under the 2MB budget. Per-feature `year` property added (the representative window label) alongside the original SRC_DATE. Attribution wording is a placeholder pending the cpra-cims-terms-of-use openQuestion below.

mpdv.searchImplementation: MPDV proxies Nominatim through its own origin at https://mpdv.coastal.la.gov/nominatim/search — i.e. it does NOT call the public nominatim.openstreetmap.org endpoint directly from the browser. Relevant for 04-SPEC's search-tool fallback chain: our site has no backend to proxy through, so a direct client-side Nominatim call (bounded to the parish, with a compliant User-Agent/Referer and conservative rate limiting per OSM's usage policy) is the closest equivalent, not a like-for-like copy of MPDV's approach.

guidedTourTranscript.method: Static extraction from the shipped, unminified-enough production JS bundle (component call arguments contain literal slide text) — Chrome automation was unavailable in this session, so this is NOT a live interactive walkthrough. Visual/interaction mechanics (dock position, animation timing, progress-dot behavior) could not be observed and should be spot-checked live before Phase 4 finalizes the player UI.
guidedTourTranscript.flow: Tour slides progress through: 1) historical land change since 1932, 2) sea-level-rise/scenario framing, 3) land-loss projection without the plan (1,100–3,000 sq mi over 50 years), 4) storm-surge flood-damage framing, 5) EADD/EASD damage metrics explained, 6) introduces the 77 selected projects, 7) land-loss avoided WITH the plan (230–310 sq mi), 8) structural risk-reduction project framing, 9) damage reduction WITH the plan, 10) closing "future coast" vision framed explicitly as a plan-dependent vision, not a guarantee.
guidedTourTranscript.exitBehavior: Tour ends by inviting the user into a separate 'Explore' mode via an "Explore the Plan" button — not a hard reset. Confirms the 05-SPEC's 'exit leaves the map where the tour left it, no hostile reset' principle is exactly what CPRA's own tool does.
guidedTourTranscript.toneNotes: Every scenario figure is paired with its environmental-scenario qualifier ("lower"/"higher" scenario) in the same sentence as the number — CPRA never states a bare projection without naming it as scenario-dependent. The Iberia tour's own copy should match this discipline exactly, per 05-SPEC's sourcing caution.
